text: Yes, the owner likely broke the law by removing trees after 2020. The evidence shows tree-cover loss events in 2021 (81.3 ha), 2022 (0.6 ha), and 2023 (4.5 ha), all confirmed by the JRC 2020 forest reference data. These losses exceed the 0.5 ha minimum event area and meet the 50% corroboration threshold. The 2021 event alone affected 2.23% of the asset, far surpassing minor or fragmented losses. Since the baseline was set at December 31, 2020, any post-2020 losses would violate regulations unless permitted. The data confirms significant, intentional deforestation after the compliance deadline.
